#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse hook: my-custom-hook
#
# Fires after a matched tool call completes. Reads the PostToolUse JSON
# payload from stdin (tool_name, tool_input, tool_response, session_id,
# transcript_path) and may emit JSON on stdout to attach additionalContext
# or an updatedToolOutput.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - success (stdout, if any, is parsed as hookSpecificOutput JSON)
#   1 - hook-internal error; fails open (non-blocking) on Claude Code and Codex
set -euo pipefail

input="$(cat)"

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # jq is a required dependency; fail open rather than block the tool call.
  exit 0
fi

tool_name="$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.tool_name // empty')"

# TODO: custom logic goes here. Inspect $input / $tool_name and, if needed,
# emit JSON like:
#   {"hookEventName": "PostToolUse", "hookSpecificOutput": {"additionalContext": "..."}}

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse-my-custom-hook.sh — Catalyst-style hook
#
# Event: PostToolUse
# Fires after a tool call completes. Input fields: tool_name, tool_input,
# tool_response, session_id, transcript_path. Output (optional): JSON on
# stdout with hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (fed back to Claude) and/or
# hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput (replaces what Claude sees as the tool
# result). A hook with nothing to say should emit no output and exit 0.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - success. No stdout => no-op. Stdout with valid JSON => processed per
#       the output fields above.
#   1 - hook-internal error (e.g. missing jq). Fail-open: non-blocking on
#       Claude Code and Codex, session continues either way.
#   2 - stderr is shown to Claude as feedback. Non-blocking for PostToolUse
#       specifically, since the tool has already run by the time this fires.
#   other non-zero - stderr is shown to the user only; execution continues.

set -euo pipefail

# Fail-open on missing jq. Must precede every jq use below.
if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 1; fi

# Read the hook payload from stdin.
INPUT="$(cat 2>/dev/null || true)"

TOOL_NAME="$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_name // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)"
TOOL_INPUT="$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -c '.tool_input // {}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
TOOL_RESPONSE="$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -c '.tool_response // {}' 2>/dev/null || true)"

# TODO: implement custom logic here. Inspect $TOOL_NAME / $TOOL_INPUT /
# $TOOL_RESPONSE and, if there's something to say, emit JSON such as:
#   jq -n --arg ctx "your message" '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PostToolUse", additionalContext: $ctx}}'
# Otherwise, produce no output.

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse-my-custom-hook.sh — Catalyst hook
#
# Event: PostToolUse
# Fires after a matched tool call completes. Input on stdin includes
# tool_name, tool_input, tool_response, session_id, transcript_path.
# Output (optional): hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext /
# hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput as JSON on stdout.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - success (with or without JSON output on stdout)
#   1 - hook-internal error (missing dependency, bad input) — fail-open,
#       non-blocking on Claude Code and Codex
#
# Test locally:
#   echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{},"tool_response":{}}' \
#     | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$PWD bash hooks/PostToolUse-my-custom-hook.sh

set -euo pipefail

# Fail-open on missing jq. Must precede every jq use below.
if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 1; fi

INPUT="$(cat 2>/dev/null || true)"
PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)}"
[ -n "$PROJECT_DIR" ] || PROJECT_DIR="$(pwd)"

TOOL_NAME="$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_name // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)"

# TODO: custom logic goes here. Inspect $INPUT / $TOOL_NAME and, if you want
# to surface something to the agent, emit JSON on stdout, e.g.:
#   jq -n --arg ctx "your message" '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PostToolUse", additionalContext: $ctx}}'
# A hook with nothing to say should exit 0 with no output.

exit 0
